questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why tech companies are abandoning A.I. data centers after local election losses
How Texas and Ohio governors plan to ban data centers from all farmland
How neoclouds are replacing Amazon and Google in data center construction
Why voter opposition will likely slow, but not stop, data center building
questions.explain: Despite strong voter opposition, analysts expect only modest cancellations and continued construction.

questions.q: In how many of 41 local ballot initiatives did citizens vote to limit or prevent data centers?
questions.explain: The passage says citizens voted to limit or prevent data centers in 40 out of 41 local initiatives.

questions.q: What did Bernstein estimate as the more realistic share of future data centers to be canceled?
questions.explain: Bernstein said more realistically only 2 to 4 percent of future data centers would be canceled.

questions.q: What did Microsoft's summer polls find about people who oppose data centers?
options: About 70 percent could accept them with protections such as tax revenue
About 15 percent would accept them only if built by union workers
About 70 percent wanted them banned from farmland and industrial sites
About half would accept them if electricity rates were frozen for residents
questions.explain: Roughly 70 percent said they could accept the buildings with protections, while nothing would satisfy about 15 percent.

questions.q: Why are neoclouds seen as more vulnerable than the biggest tech firms?
options: They are barred from building in any state with a moratorium
They have taken on more debt than the industry giants
They rely more heavily on union labor than their larger rivals
They do not train A.I. models for large paying customers
questions.explain: The passage says neoclouds have taken on more debt than giants, who have the resources to navigate the changes.
